messages:
maya: heads up — I just hit a nasty routing gap with workspace-claim tokens + our ejection circuit breaker. a customer with a private VPC and a workspace claim got ejected from their dedicated pool and fell back to hosted. hosted accepted the request but quota scoping didn’t follow — tokens were counted under the org quota, not the workspace one. noticed around 11:12 in prod logs.

alex: ugh. can you paste the raw routing log?

maya: pasted below. short version: router decided `workspace=ws-682` -> tried pool `dedicated-g4-ws682` -> circuit breaker ejected (capacity) -> fallback `hosted-small` -> request routed without `x-workspace` scoping attr, so billing/quotas used org-level.

maya: ```
[2024-10-03T11:12:14Z] router.decide request_id=rb-9a2 ws_claim=x-claim:ws-682 pool=d-g4-ws682 -> eject(reason=capacity) -> fallback=hosted-small routing_attrs={pool:hosted-small} 
[2024-10-03T11:12:14Z] router.emit_scope request_id=rb-9a2 scope=org:acme corp (missing: workspace)
```

chris: quick q — do we still strip workspace headers on fallback for isolation reasons? i thought that was the safety behavior to avoid leaking private endpoint routing.

maya: we do a header scrub when fallback crosses private/public boundary, but in this case the fallback stayed within the customer's private endpoint (same VPC) because hosted-small is on their private pool. the problem is our scope attribution logic uses `routing_attrs` not the original claim header when computing quota key. after ejection we only have pool=hosted-small.

alex: hmm. two separate problems: 1) policy: whether workspace claim should be authoritative even after pool ejection, and 2) implementation: ensure scope attr is preserved or a derived workspace tag is attached to the fallback route.

teresa: +1 on making claim authoritative if the claim is verified and the fallback is still within private customer boundary. otherwise we expose cross-tenant risk. we need a conservative rule: if fallback.endpoint.is_private==true && claim_verified==true => preserve workspace scope.

nina: telemetry note — we currently emit `routing.ejection` metric with tags (pool, reason). need to add `preserved_claim=true/false` and `resulting_scope` so we can measure how often scoping is lost. also add `routing.decision_debug` event for sampled traces.

chris: small UX ask: add a console flag under rollout > routing called `preserve_workspace_on_fallback` (off by default). team can toggle during rollout for canary orgs. should be behind a kill-switch.

alex: implementation plan suggestion:
- attach `workspace_id` to the request context as part of claim verification step (before pool selection)
- when ejection happens, router checks: if fallback.is_private && context.workspace_id != null -> copy context.workspace_id into routing_attrs.scope
- if fallback.is_public -> scrub workspace and log event for manual review

maya: + proposed change to metrics: new counter `routing.scope_loss.count` with tags reason=(ejection|auth|scrub) and sample a 1% debug trace for `routing.decision` with full headers.

teresa: need to add a privacy review for debug traces. SRE and security signoff before enabling sampling on production.

sre-bot: deploy triggered: branch=feat/preserve-workspace-on-fallback, env=staging, id=deploy-8873

alex: i'll pick up the router/context change (INF-4321). chris can you add the console toggle + rollout page notes (INF-4322)? nina can you own telemetry schema + dashboards (INF-4323). teresa will coordinate privacy/security review (INF-4324). maya will validate against the production example.

maya: thanks. putting the logs and a short repro in the ticket. will add a short test that simulates pool ejection and ensures the workspace_id is attached to resulting scope.

chris: one more edge case — if claim is stale (expired) but still present, we should prefer ejection and not preserve. add a `claim_valid_until` check.

alex: agreed. auth layer must surface `claim_status` (valid|expired|revoked) to the router.

nina: noted for dashboards: show `routing.scope_loss.count` over time + top orgs affected. will add alert if > 5 events/min across prod.

teresa: thanks everyone. adding privacy reviewers to INF-4324: @security-team @privacy.

maya: closing for now — action items in tickets. will follow up after staging deploy. :thumbsup:
